html:
Marko Mrnjavčević, called Prince Marko or King Marko, was a Serbian king who ruled a small realm around Prilep in today's North Macedonia from 1371 until his death in 1395.

After his father died in battle against the Ottomans at the Maritsa in 1371, Marko became an Ottoman vassal and died fighting for the sultan against Wallachia at the Battle of Rovine. History remembers little of him, but epic poetry made him the greatest hero of the Balkans: a giant of a man who rides a piebald horse, drinks wine by the bucket and fights Turks and monsters. Serbs, Macedonians and Bulgarians all sing of him. The ruins of his fortress tower over Prilep in North Macedonia.
sum: Marko Mrnjavčević, called Prince Marko or King Marko, was a Serbian king who ruled a small realm around Prilep in today's North Macedonia from 1371 until his death in 1395.
